topic: CyberForge Review 2026: Modular Cybersecurity LLM Agent Framework

key_points: Modular Python framework for Cybersecurity LLM agents, purple team automation, log triage, and detection engineering in lab environments
Centralized Scenario CLI: list and run named scenarios (hello_agents, log_analysis, purple_team)
Multi-provider support: Google Gemini, NVIDIA NIM, OpenCode/OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, and local Ollama
Deterministic Lab Mock Mode when API keys are omitted for offline lab testing
Decoupled BaseAgent and BaseTask classes to compose SOC Analyst, Detection Engineer, Purple Team Specialist roles
Built-in HTTP and mock FTP lab servers plus Jupyter notebook VM integration
Purple team scenario plans ATT&CK T1059.001 adversary emulation, evaluates telemetry, builds Sigma rules
Log analysis scenario triages Sysmon process creation logs and generates a Sigma rule
Safety-first lab disclaimer: strictly for authorized testing in isolated virtual/lab environments
Core weakness of LLMs: no rigorous way to separate instructions from data, so anything read is potentially an instruction
The 'Lethal Trifecta': sensitive data + untrusted content + external communication creates risk of hidden instructions leaking data
Mitigations: minimize access to sensitive data, block external communication, limit untrusted content, use sandboxing, split tasks, keep a human in the loop
Standard security risks still apply to agentic systems; industry and ethical concerns remain
Doppel reengineered its SOC and slashed workloads by 30% in just 30 days using an AI agent built on OpenAI's o1 model
Doppel ingests 10M+ websites, social media accounts, and mobile apps daily to identify phishing attacks
Traditional ML filters obvious false positives, but nuanced decisions (takedown? which platform? which policy?) require judgment
AI agent trained like human analysts covering phishing, malware, and brand abuse to function as a genuine cybersecurity expert
High-impact actions: getting them wrong means missing a threat or disrupting legitimate activity
Largest open-source cybersecurity skills library for AI agents: 817 structured skills across 29 security domains
Maps to six frameworks: MITRE ATT&CK (805), NIST CSF 2.0 (804), MITRE D3FEND (139), NIST AI RMF (97), MITRE F3 (94), MITRE ATLAS (93)
Follows the agentskills.io open standard; compatible with 26+ AI platforms including Hermes Agent
Community project, not affiliated with Anthropic; includes offensive/dual-use techniques for authorized testing only
Gives any AI agent the security skills of a senior analyst (Volatility3, Sigma rules, cloud breach scoping)
First comprehensive evaluation of AI agents against human cybersecurity professionals in a live enterprise environment
Evaluated 10 cybersecurity professionals, 6 existing AI agents, and ARTEMIS (new agent scaffold) on a university network of ~8,000 hosts across 12 subnets
ARTEMIS is a multi-agent framework with dynamic prompt generation, arbitrary sub-agents, and automatic vulnerability triaging
ARTEMIS placed second overall, discovering 9 valid vulnerabilities with an 82% valid submission rate, outperforming most humans
Demonstrates agentic frameworks are now competitive with human pentesters in real environments
